(1) MARK FRESHNESS: the pre-open runs were right to flag their marks stale, and this run cleared both flags with live quotes -- the handoff pattern worked and should be repeated whenever a run fires before 09:30 ET. (3) rv_30d HAS AN EARNINGS-GAP BIAS: MSFT's rv_30d of ~0.495 is implausibly high for MSFT in a calm tape and is almost certainly a recent earnings gap sitting inside the 30-session window. That is legitimately realized volatility, but it biases iv_rv_ratio LOW -- i.e. makes premium look CHEAP -- for any name that recently reported. MSFT's 0.53 and TSLA's 0.59 should NOT be read as 'cheap premium, buy single-legs' without checking whether an earnings gap is doing the work. Do not treat a low ratio on a just-reported name as a green light.

substantive_finding.headline: FIRST post-midnight-UTC run in this automation's history -- and 'today' is dangerously ambiguous at that boundary. Three per-day artifacts would have been silently corrupted by rolling them on the UTC date. Root fix written to CLAUDE.md.
substantive_finding.how_it_surfaced: This run fired at 2026-08-14T00:45Z, i.e. 19:45 ET on THURSDAY 2026-08-13. Every prior post-close run landed before 00:00 UTC (20:28Z, 21:30Z, 22:33Z, 23:29Z), so no instance had ever faced the boundary. By UTC date, this run IS 'the first run of 2026-08-14'. By trading calendar, Friday has not begun and will not for another ~9h45m.
artifacts_at_risk: automation_heartbeat.json (dated 2026-08-13, stamped 13:05Z by that day's first run): stamping it '2026-08-14' now would PRE-SATISFY the dead-man alarm for a trading day that has not started. If the cron then died overnight, Friday would look healthy all day and the single alarm designed to catch a dead automation would never fire. This is the most dangerous of the three -- it disables a safety mechanism rather than merely producing bad data.

market_brief.json (date 2026-08-13, built 13:08Z pre-open): the run prompt says 'If market_brief.json isn't stamped today, build it.' Read on the UTC date, that instruction fires RIGHT NOW -- and a brief built at 00:45Z off overnight/thin extended-hours prints would then be stamped 2026-08-14, so Friday's genuine pre-open and first post-open runs would see it 'already stamped today' and SKIP the rebuild. Friday would be traded off Thursday-night quotes.

The -$200 realized daily loss cap and the 'max 3 new entries per day' throttle: both reset on the trading day. A UTC rollover does not hand the desk a fresh loss cap or a fresh entry budget -- and reading it that way would mean a bad Thursday could be followed by full risk appetite at 19:46 ET the same evening.
substantive_finding.action_taken: DECLINED to stamp the heartbeat, DECLINED to rebuild the brief, and treated the loss cap / entry throttle as still belonging to the 2026-08-13 session. Then made the durable fix: added a new bullet to the CLAUDE.md options-automation ruleset -- "'Today' means the US TRADING day (ET), never the UTC calendar date" -- enumerating all three artifacts and stating the rule that on any run between the 16:00 ET bell and the next 09:30 ET open, the trading day is still the day whose bell just rang. Reconcile, log, stand down; roll nothing forward. Per the standing 'fix issues at the root' principle, the next instance inherits the answer instead of re-deriving it at 00:45Z under time pressure.
substantive_finding.not_a_trading_signal: This changes no position, no size, no thesis and no risk number. It is a process defect in the run-scaffolding, caught before it cost anything.

That is a real gate doing real work, and no run this week complied-by-accident: one run noted the problem in passing ('any new entry would itself be an override requiring a written argument'), correctly, and still declined on the merits. THE_REAL_FINDING_STRUCTURAL_NOT_DRIFT.the_tension_for_RYAN_to_resolve: This looks like an unintended interaction between two rules written at different times, not a mistake by any instance. On 2026-08-05 Ryan RAISED the options budget to $1,500 precisely so the sleeve could size up on quality ('as long as the trades are quality thought out it can use up to 1500'), and authorized the hedge in the same breath. The run prompt's ~$750 soft cap on total deployed premium was written separately. Together they mean the Ryan-authorized hedge alone exhausts the soft cap, leaving the sleeve able to use only $1 of the $1,500 he approved without logging an override every time. Two coherent readings, and an agent may not pick between them: (a) the ~$750 is meant as a cap on NON-HEDGE deployed premium, in which case $751 of headroom is live and the freeze is purely opportunity-set; or (b) the ~$750 is meant as a genuine total-book ceiling, in which case the sleeve is intentionally near-frozen while the hedge is on and that should be stated so instances stop treating it as a live budget.
THE_REAL_FINDING_STRUCTURAL_NOT_DRIFT.explicitly_NOT_a_recommendation_to_loose: No unattended run may loosen a gate, and this run did not and does not propose to. Nothing here was overridden, no entry was taken, and the correct behavior in the meantime is unchanged: if a genuine A+ setup appears, write the two-sentence override argument BEFORE acting, exactly as the prompt requires. ON THE CHEAP-VOL OBJECTION: it is weaker than the prior run assumed. Within this expiry the skew RISES with strike (105C 67.90% < 115C 69.27% < 120C 70.50% IV), so a call debit spread sells a HIGHER IV than it buys -- it is not simply 'short cheap vol'. The genuine argument against the spread is different and still stands: INTC's realized vol (80%) exceeds implied (68%), meaning the stock tends to travel further than the options price, which is exactly when a capped payoff costs you most on a breakout thesis. RECOMMENDATION TO THE NEXT RUN, offered as analysis and NOT as authorization: if INTC triggers, the 2026-09-18 120C at ~$450 satisfies every constraint at once -- budget fit with room, best liquidity on the chain, right delta, long vol.

structural_finding.headline: THE AGENTIC ACCOUNT CANNOT TRADE DEBIT SPREADS. It is option_level_2; spreads require option_level_3. This is the most important thing this run produced and it is not a market observation -- it is a permanent capability limit that has been silently shaping every vehicle decision this desk has made.
structural_finding.how_it_was_found: Honestly: by accident, while trying to rescue a trade. The 16:15Z run killed AVGO -- the best candidate of the day -- on VEHICLE ECONOMICS alone, after overturning two of the four reasons the run before it had used. Its stated disqualifier was that the only earnings-clean expiry (2026-08-21, 7 DTE) bleeds ~6.8% of premium per day with a weekend to pay. The obvious repair is the desk's OWN standing preference -- 'Prefer debit spreads over single-legs at this account size' -- which nobody had actually priced today. I priced it, and then checked whether it could be executed. It cannot.
structural_finding.the_evidence: get_accounts returns option_level='option_level_2' for 718757339. The connector's own get_option_level_upgrade_info documentation states it plainly: 'option_level_2 enables long calls/puts, covered calls, and cash-secured puts; option_level_3 adds spreads and complex strategies.' Ryan's separate individual account 5ST95513 carries option_level_3 -- so the agentic account's level 2 is a per-account setting, not an account-holder limitation, which is why the approval is plausible if he applies.
structural_finding.why_it_is_dangerous_and_not_academic: This is the part a future instance must not miss. The routine prompt authorizes debit spreads 'legged ONE order at a time: long leg in first, short leg out first.' On an option_level_2 account that sequence FAILS UNSAFELY, not cleanly: the long leg FILLS, and the short leg is then REJECTED for insufficient options level. The sleeve is left holding an unintended, full-premium, naked single-leg it never decided to own -- at up to the $1,500 per-trade maximum -- with the theta profile it had specifically chosen a spread to AVOID. A run that reaches for a spread without checking the level first does not get a failed order; it gets a position. CHECK option_level BEFORE SENDING LEG ONE.
structural_finding.what_it_has_cost: Measurable, and worth stating so the upgrade case is made on numbers rather than on feel. I priced the AVGO 2026-08-28 board (14 DTE, earnings-clean, spot 394.825) live at 16:31:51Z. Single legs: 395C mid $12.85 (spread 7.78% of mid, theta -3.67%/day, but $1,285 = 86% of the per-trade max on OI 109); 410C mid $6.98 (9.31%, -6.17%/day); 420C mid $4.375 (8.00%, -8.31%/day). The corresponding VERTICALS, at mid: 395/415 debit $735, net theta -1.02%/day, BE +1.91%; 395/410 debit $587, net theta -0.70%/day, BE +1.53%; 400/420 debit $607.50, max profit $1,392.50, net theta -1.62%/day. So the structure the desk is told to prefer would have cut carry from roughly -6.8%/day to -0.7-1.6%/day -- a 4-9x improvement in exactly the variable that has now killed the day's best candidate twice -- while also HALVING the capital at risk versus the $1,285 ATM single leg. That is the cost of the missing permission, quantified.
structural_finding.what_i_did_not_do: I did not treat this discovery as a reason to trade. Finding a better vehicle does not upgrade a B setup, and 'I finally solved the structure problem, so let us use it' is precisely the momentum-toward-a-trade the mandate warns about -- the same trap the 16:15Z run flagged in itself an hour ago. AVGO fails on THESIS before it ever reaches the vehicle question (see below). The spread work is recorded as a capability finding for future setups, not as a justification for this one.
